answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring each identity to build a long, verifiable thread of completed work before it gains influence. Like an onyx ledger entry, that history cannot be copied or bought: new accounts start with no voting weight, earn trust only through successful, checkable tasks over time, and lock a small refundable bond that is slashed for fraud. A jade mark of seniority is therefore expensive in time, not just identities, so an attacker spinning up thousands of fakes gains no power until each fake has done real, costly work.
